extracted.intended_audience: Members of the public, stakeholders, and regulated entities who want to review or submit comments on Texas DPS proposed rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for participating in Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) rulemaking: where rules are published, how long the public comment period lasts, how and where to submit written comments, and how to register for adoption notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of DPS rules in the Texas Administrative Code
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Administrative Code (TAC) is a compilation of all state agency rules in Texas. The Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) rules are located under Texas Administrative Code, Title 37, Part 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies where adopted DPS rules will be codified and where interested parties can consult the agency's rules in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of publication in the Texas Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules are published in the Texas Register to give the public notice of a state agency's proposed rulemaking action and to allow interested individuals an opportunity to review and make comments on the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication in the Texas Register is the legal/public notice mechanism that triggers the opportunity to participate in rulemaking; stakeholders should monitor the Texas Register to know when a proposal is available for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment period length
rubrics_metrics.description: The public comment period begins on the date the notice is published in the Texas Register and lasts for 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing of participation is tied to the publication date; counting of the 30-day period starts on the publication date in the Texas Register. Plan to submit within this window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment receipt deadline/time
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments on proposed rules must be received no later than 5 p.m. on the 30th day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deadline is strict as to receipt (not just postmark). Ensure delivery method will result in receipt by the agency by 5:00 p.m. on the final day of the comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required form/method of comment submission
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit a comment by sending them in writing to the agency representative indicated in the preamble of each proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be written and directed to the specific agency representative named in the proposal preamble; check each proposal’s preamble for the correct recipient and address/instructions (mail, email, or other specified means).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to receive notifications of adopted rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To be notified when rules are adopted in the Texas Register, visit the Secretary of State site to register for email notification at: http://sos.state.tx.us/texreg/subinfo.shtml
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders who want automatic updates about adoptions should register at the Secretary of State’s Texas Register notification page to receive email alerts rather than monitoring manually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document metadata (last updated)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page includes a 'last updated' date which helps users know the currency of the guidance and listings; check this to ensure you are using up-to-date procedural information.
